This time the youth minister began by expressing concern but relied on open questions and reflective listening to build rapport and encourage Tommy to share his experiences. Tommy provided a great deal of useful information regarding his drinking very quickly, which set the stage for a more productive conversation. By exploring both sides of the issue, Tommy was given the opportunity to open up without fear of condemnation, and was also able to admit to some of the consequences of his drinking. This gave him the chance to consider the reasons he might benefit from making a change. The youth minister also encouraged Tommy to look ahead to consider how his drinking could affect his future plans. By exploring his values and relating them to his drinking, she developed a discrepancy between his future goals and his current behaviors, highlighting the need to make some adjustments to his drinking. Using a summary, the youth minister was able to transition smoothly to a discussion of options, and Tommy identified a realistic goal for himself that matched his values. As a result, he is much more likely to follow through on his plans and actually make a change in his drinking.
